City garden opens its gates

The city garden opened its gates on Saturday morning with music and food stalls for every visitor.

Children planted sunflower seeds along the main path while volunteers handed out paper maps of the beds.

The mayor cut the ribbon at noon and thanked the gardeners who worked through the spring rain.

Visiting hours

The garden welcomes visitors every day from nine in the morning until sunset.

On Mondays the gates open one hour later so the gardeners can water the north beds.

On Tuesdays a guided walk leaves the main gate at ten and returns before lunch.

On Wednesdays the rose house stays open late for the evening scent tour.

On Thursdays school groups book the classroom shed for planting lessons.

On Fridays the market stalls sell honey, apples and bunches of cut flowers.

On Saturdays the lawn hosts picnics and the pond rents small rowing boats.

On Sundays the choir sings under the old oak tree at four in the afternoon.
